skill.name: mcp-builder
skill.description: Guide for planning, building, and evaluating MCP servers that connect AI agents to external APIs through well-designed tools.
skill.summary: Build Python or TypeScript MCP servers with focused tools, validation, documentation, and evaluation workflows.
skill.author: ComposioHQ

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown examples, TypeScript template literals, placeholder secrets, and public documentation URLs. The real security concern is the evaluation harness, which can launch or connect to user-supplied MCP servers while forwarding headers or environment variables. No evidence found of prompt injection intended to influence this marketplace audit.

remediation.issue: The evaluation harness can run user-supplied commands and connect to user-supplied MCP endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must evaluate only trusted servers, and recommend sandboxing local stdio targets before passing credentials.

remediation.issue: Environment variables and HTTP headers can contain credentials that are forwarded to evaluated servers.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to pass only minimum required secrets, avoid real credentials for untrusted targets, and redact secrets from reports and logs.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes placeholder API keys and tokens that static scanners flag as secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders clearly non-real and add a short note that example credentials must be replaced with user-managed secrets.

semantic_findings.description: The evaluation CLI accepts a command, arguments, URL, headers, and environment values, then connects to or launches that MCP server. This is expected functionality, but it can run untrusted code or forward secrets if users evaluate an untrusted server.

content.value_statement: MCP server design is difficult because agents need focused tools, clear schemas, and reliable evaluations. This skill guides planning, implementation, testing, and evaluation for Python and TypeScript MCP servers.
actual_capabilities: Guides agent-centered MCP tool design for real workflows instead of simple endpoint wrappers.
Explains Python FastMCP and TypeScript SDK implementation patterns.
Recommends schema validation with Pydantic or Zod and clear tool annotations.
Provides an evaluation workflow for testing whether agents can use MCP tools effectively.
Includes helper scripts for connecting to stdio, SSE, and HTTP MCP servers during evaluation.
limitations: It is a development guide, not a complete generated MCP server for a specific service.
Users must supply service documentation, credentials, and API requirements.
Evaluation scripts can run user-supplied MCP servers, so only trusted targets should be tested.
External documentation links may change and should be verified before implementation.

use_cases.description: Plan tool names, schemas, response formats, and shared utilities before writing server code.

use_cases.title: Implement a Python or TypeScript Server
use_cases.description: Follow language-specific guidance for validation, async API calls, error handling, and server setup.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Tool Use
use_cases.description: Create realistic read-only questions and run them through an MCP evaluation harness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an MCP Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new API integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan an MCP server for this API. Identify the most useful agent workflows, tool names, inputs, outputs, and evaluation questions.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Python Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a FastMCP implementation from a plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the MCP builder guidance, create a Python FastMCP server for these workflows. Include Pydantic input models and clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a TypeScript Server
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a TypeScript MCP SDK implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the MCP builder guidance, create a TypeScript MCP server with Zod schemas, strict typing, useful annotations, and concise responses.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate and Improve Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this MCP server and evaluation file. Find gaps in tool design, validation, response size, error messages, and test coverage.

Recommended input fields, validation rules, and response formats.
A set of read-only evaluation questions for agent testing.

output_examples.input: Review my TypeScript MCP server before release.
output: Findings about schema coverage, annotations, and error handling.
Suggestions to reduce response size and improve pagination.
A short checklist for build and evaluation readiness.

output_examples.input: Create evaluations for a new support ticket MCP server.
output: Ten realistic read-only questions with stable expected answers.
Guidance for verifying answers manually before running the harness.
Recommendations for removing destructive or unstable tasks.

best_practices: Start with user workflows and implement only tools that help agents complete real tasks.
Use strict input validation, clear annotations, and concise responses by default.
Run evaluations with trusted servers and avoid forwarding unnecessary secrets.
anti_patterns: Do not expose every API endpoint as a separate tool without workflow design.
Do not return unbounded data dumps when pagination or summaries would work.
Do not run evaluation targets or pass credentials unless the server is trusted.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete MCP server automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning, implementation, and evaluation. The user still supplies API details and project requirements.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Python with FastMCP and TypeScript with the official MCP SDK.

faq.question: Can it help with evaluation design?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to create read-only tasks, verify answers, and run the included evaluation harness.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: It recommends fetching official MCP documentation and can evaluate remote MCP servers when the user provides a URL.

faq.question: How should credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Use the minimum required secrets, pass them only to trusted servers, and avoid storing them in evaluation files.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production integrations?
faq.answer: It can guide production-quality work, but users must still review security, authentication, rate limits, and deployment controls.
